topic_ko: 애도 작업 — 슬픔을 존중하며 행동으로 이끄는 힘
_note: 유형별 묶음 구조. 같은 33번 지문이라도 유형마다 passage를 다르게 paraphrase 한다.

passage: Across psychology, theorists concur that mourning our losses matters, whether those losses are private or shared by a whole community.
Grief is not a frozen feeling but a moving process that consciousness cannot do without.
Psychologically, it lets us confront our own fragility and that of others, and it restores our energy after serious loss.
Mourning pays respect to the sorrow and the sense of absence rather than pushing them aside.
At the same time it prepares the soil in which personal change and continued life can take root.
One psychotherapist calls this work an act of devotion grounded in love, one that demands continual attention and listening.
Grieving what has gone opens a path toward deeper love for whatever still remains with us.
In time that love becomes a wish to repair the damage done, or to make amends for it.
choices: why psychologists disagree about how long mourning should last
how grief both honours sorrow and generates a drive to repair
why personal losses affect people more deeply than collective ones
how listening carefully can reduce the pain of a serious loss
why energy levels naturally decline after a significant bereavement
theme.explanation_ko: 애도가 슬픔을 존중하면서 동시에 남은 것에 대한 사랑과 복구 의지를 만들어 낸다는 것이 주제이다. ②가 정답.
theme.distractor_ko: ①애도 기간 논쟁, ③개인 대 집단 상실 비교, ④경청의 효과, ⑤에너지 감소는 본문의 초점이 아니다.

passage: We should not treat grief as a weakness to be cut short or hurried past.
Psychological theory agrees that mourning matters for both private and shared losses.
Grief is a moving process that consciousness genuinely requires.
It lets us face our own fragility and restores our energy after serious loss.
Mourning honours the sorrow instead of denying it, while preparing the ground for change.
Grieving what is gone deepens our love for whatever still remains.
That deepened love gradually becomes a wish to repair the damage or make amends.
We should therefore give grief the time and attention it needs rather than rushing to move on.
choices: 상실의 슬픔은 가능한 한 빨리 잊고 일상으로 돌아가야 한다.
심리학 이론은 실제 상담 현장의 경험보다 우선시되어야 한다.
애도는 서둘러 끝낼 것이 아니라 충분한 시간과 주의를 들여야 한다.
집단적 상실은 개인적 상실보다 더 우선적으로 다뤄져야 한다.
손상을 복구하려는 시도는 애도가 완전히 끝난 뒤에 시작해야 한다.
claim.explanation_ko: 애도가 슬픔을 존중하며 변화와 복구 의지의 토대를 만들므로 서둘러 끝낼 것이 아니라 충분히 거쳐야 한다는 주장이다. ③이 정답.
claim.distractor_ko: ①빠른 망각, ②이론 우선, ④집단 상실 우선, ⑤복구 시점 제한은 본문 주장과 어긋난다.

passage: Theories throughout psychology agree that mourning our losses matters, private or collective.
Grief is a moving emotional process without which consciousness cannot function well.
It helps us look directly at fragility, impermanence and death, and it restores energy after loss.
Grief work honours the sorrow and the felt absence rather than brushing them aside.
At the same time it prepares the ground for personal transformation and for life to go on.

In time this becomes a desire to repair as much damage as we can, or to compensate for it.
choices: Forgetting Faster: A Practical Guide to Moving On

The Two Faces of Grief: Deep Sorrow and the Will to Repair
